title: The Global Minimum Tax, Investment Incentives and Asymmetric Tax Competition
abstract: arXiv:2409.05397v4 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: This paper investigates the OECD's global minimum tax (GMT) in a formal model of tax competition between asymmetric countries. We consider both profit shifting and real responses of multinational enterprises, and highlight the role of the substance-based income exclusion (SBIE) in investment incentives and tax rate setting. The GMT reduces the true tax rate differential and benefits the large country, while the revenue effect is generally ambiguous for the small country. In the short run where tax rates are fixed, the GMT reduces the small country's revenue if profit shifting costs are low and increases it otherwise. In the long run where countries adjust tax rates, the GMT reshapes the tax game and the competition pattern. We reveal that the minimum rate binds the small country only if it is low. With the rise of the GMT rate, countries will set tax rates below the minimum to boost capital investments and collect top-up taxes. Simul

translated_title: 全球最低税、投资激励与非对称税收竞争
translated_abstract: 本文在一个非对称国家间税收竞争的形式化模型中研究了OECD的全球最低税（GMT）。我们同时考虑了利润转移和跨国企业的实际反应，并强调实质所得排除（SBIE）在投资激励与税率设定中的作用。全球最低税缩小了真实税率差异并使大国受益，而其对小国财政收入的影响通常是不确定的。在税率固定的短期中，若利润转移成本较低，全球最低税会减少小国的财政收入，否则会增加其财政收入。在各国调整税率的长期中，全球最低税重塑了税收博弈与竞争格局。我们揭示，只有当最低税率较低时，它才会对小国形成约束。随着全球最低税率的上升，各国将把税率设定在最低线之下，以促进资本投资并征收补充税。
tldr: 本文通过非对称国家税收竞争模型研究OECD全球最低税，发现其缩小真实税率差异并有利于大国，短期内对小国财政收入的影响取决于利润转移成本高低，长期则重塑税收竞争格局——当最低税率较高时，各国会将法定税率设定在最低线以下以刺激投资并征收补充税。
en_tdlr: Using a formal model of tax competition between asymmetric countries, this paper shows that the OECD global minimum tax narrows true tax rate differentials and benefits the large country, has ambiguous short-run revenue effects on the small country depending on profit-shifting costs, and reshapes long-run tax competition by inducing countries to set tax rates below the minimum to boost investment and collect top-up taxes.
